summary: Daniel (Greek) 11 (45 verses) continues the story of faithfulness. Starting with '“As for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to confirm and strengthen him.', it moves through themes of faithfulness, wisdom and calls readers toward hope.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows faithfulness lived out in second temple period. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: “As for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to confirm and strengthen him.
After the treaty is made with him, he will work deceitfully; for he will come up, and will become strong with a small people.
He will plant the tents of his palace between the sea and the glorious holy mountain; yet he will come to his end, and no one will help him.

questions.question: What is happening in Daniel (Greek) 11?
questions.answer: In 45 verses, this chapter daniel (greek) 11 (45 verses) continues the story of faithfulness. starting with '“as for me, in the first year of darius the mede, i stood up to confirm and strengthen him.', it moves through themes of faithfulness, wisdom and calls readers toward hope. The setting is second temple period, written to jewish community. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote Daniel (Greek) and why 11 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally anonymous / tradition, addressed to jewish community around intertestamental. This chapter fits the book's purpose as jewish literature — its themes of faithfulness, wisdom build on what came before.

questions.question: What does 'covenant' mean in this chapter?
questions.answer: Binding promise/agreement God makes with people. In this chapter, it appears in context of faithfulness. For a first-time reader: think of it as binding promise/agreement god makes with people, not just religious jargon.

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through faithfulness and wisdom, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 6 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'At the end of years they will join themselves together. The daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an agreement, but she will not retain the s...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about faithfulness. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
